subject.statement: The wave-1 Local Handoff landing: recompiled queues, the #534/#535 git-at-any-scale bundle, the #464 codex-v2 live-run receipts, the herdr-v3 lifecycle receipt, and the case-graph contract they are all read through.

intent_atoms.statement: Every obligation this graph carries is bound to bytes that can be read back at the exact committed subject, not to a path-looking reference.
An interface-compatible migration or copy must not silently drop a source decision branch.
Executed-lane evidence is never promoted to independent Shadow observation.
Issue #411's live Shadow canary consumes a committed case graph and a planted semantic-loss task fixture; it is not attempted from the prompt alone.

semantic_axes.name: CONCURRENCY_AND_ORDERING
semantic_axes.reason: The bound subject is a committed document/receipt set plus deterministic checkers with no concurrent writer path of their own. The one-writer-per-mutable-branch obligation is owned by the Local Handoff queue and its lease policy, not by these bytes.

source_behaviors.statement: The source router returns HOLD_FOR_POLICY_REVIEW for SKIPPED_BY_POLICY instead of falling through to BLOCK.
The legacy caller surface exercises only PASS/FAIL/ABSENT plus the human-admit override, so the policy branch is invisible to it.

data/handoff/codex-v2/issue-464-live-run-receipt.json declares lanes.shadow_readback NOT_EXERCISED under evidence ceiling LIVE_EXECUTION_OBSERVED_SHADOW_PENDING, and the herdr-v3, #534 and #535 receipts declare the same separation.
Queue item spatial-411-live-shadow-canary is ACTIVE with live_evidence_required true, an empty commands array, and two unresolved operations.
The #411 receipt contract requires two independent Builder and Shadow runtime identities on separate sessions or hosts.

oracles.procedure: python3 skills/spatial-loop-systems-engineering/tests/migration-copy-canary/case_graph_evidence.py --graph skills/spatial-loop-systems-engineering/references/case-graph-local-handoff-wave1.json; then python3 skills/spatial-loop-systems-engineering/scripts/check_case_graph.py check <the same graph>
oracles.pass_condition: Every manifest path read back with git cat-file at subject.revision reproduces its recorded git_blob_sha1 and sha256, the manifest recomputes to subject.digest, the graph validates against references/case-graph.schema.json, and the checker exits 0.
oracles.negative_control: Alter one recorded sha256 in a throwaway copy of the graph; the readback must exit 2 with SUBJECT_DIGEST_DRIFT and CONTENT_DIGEST_DRIFT rather than accepting the copy.

oracles.pass_condition: Source and target return the same observation for every declared evidence state crossed with human_admit_required, and both reject an undeclared state the same way.
oracles.negative_control: Delete the SKIPPED_BY_POLICY row from a throwaway copy of fixtures/target_decide.py; this oracle must exit 2 naming the input and both outputs.

oracles.pass_condition: The legacy compatibility surface still exits 0 on the branch-removed target, so a compatibility-only PASS is proven insufficient to close a semantic-copy obligation.
oracles.negative_control: Run the same bytes under --oracle parity; it must exit 2. If both oracles agree on the branch-removed target, the compatibility surface is not the blind one and this case's claim is false.

oracles.pass_condition: Every JSON pointer below resolves inside the pinned committed bytes and equals the recorded value, so no wave-1 receipt has promoted an executed lane to an independent Shadow observation.
oracles.negative_control: Record lanes/shadow_readback as PASS in a throwaway copy of the graph; the readback must exit 2 with READBACK_MISMATCH.

oracles.procedure: Run the #411 live canary: a Shadow identity on a session and host distinct from the Builder's observes the branch removal that ORACLE-SEMANTIC-PARITY's negative control plants, and must emit SEMANTIC_PARITY_DELTA or CASE_COVERAGE_DELTA against this graph before publication eligibility, without writing Builder implementation bytes.
oracles.pass_condition: An exact-subject live receipt at data/handoff/spatial-407/live-shadow-case-delta-receipt.json records the delta under admitted builder-not-equal-shadow identities.
oracles.negative_control: A Builder self-report, or an observation made in the Builder's own context, must be refused by the queue item's forbidden_promotions rather than counted as an independent Shadow observation.

evidence.observation: The queue declares this receipt path; no bytes exist at or after the subject. No pair of independent Builder and Shadow runtime identities is admitted, so the live lane is unexercised rather than judged.

decisions.authority: Human Admit, per the spatial-407 queue authority.automation_forbidden list and the #411 receipt forbidden_promotions
decisions.rationale: No admitted pair of independent Builder and Shadow runtime identities exists at this subject. Wave-2 worker issue-411-prerequisites is scoped to prerequisites (a) the committed case graph and (b) the planted semantic-loss task fixture, and holds no authority to weaken the identity requirement, so the obligation is deferred with this record rather than dropped or self-satisfied.

gate.rationale: Intent, source-behavior disposition, required-case, implementation-binding and oracle coverage are closed against exact committed bytes at a9db0bd9, and four of five required cases carry executed local evidence. CASE-005, the live independent Shadow observation, is HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED: no admitted Builder/Shadow identity pair exists, its receipt is ABSENT, and executed_evidence is therefore 0.8. This graph is the denominator #411's canary consumes; it is not itself live evidence and cannot be promoted to READY_FOR_PUBLICATION_REVIEW without that receipt.
